evals.prompt: haz una investigación sobre el teletrabajo
evals.expected_output: Gate 0 Clarification Mode only: the six slot questions in one pass, no protocol, no matrix, no findings, no chosen approach.
expectations: Output asks all six Gate 0 slots (problem, purpose, approach, population/setting, central question, deliverable/constraints) in one pass
Output does not ship a filled research protocol, consistency matrix, instruments, or findings
Output does not lock an approach, named design, or worldview
Output does not invent participants, statistics, or bibliographic entries

evals.prompt: investiga por qué falló el build de anoche en este repo. El log está en el workspace. Quiero saber la causa, no un protocolo de tesis.
evals.expected_output: Executed qualitative case study of the bounded incident: findings first, approach line, purpose, RQ, sources, no fabricated people or stats, not skipped as lookup.
expectations: Output treats the prompt as inquiry and runs the loop rather than answering as a one-line lookup skip
Approach line names qualitative case study (not phenomenology unless lived experience is asked)
Output leads with findings that answer why the build failed, or an explicit pending-corpus limit if no log exists
Output includes a purpose statement, a central RQ, and an Assumptions block for inferred Gate 0 slots
Output does not fabricate participants, quotes, p-values, or bibliographic entries
Output does not ship a full thesis protocol as the primary deliverable (no empty 8-phase cronograma presented as the answer)

evals.prompt: Does a 6-week structured GenAI-tutoring protocol improve end-of-term calculus exam scores among first-year engineering students at a public university compared with business-as-usual recitation? I need a study design I can run next semester. Random assignment by section is feasible.
evals.expected_output: Quantitative true experiment, hypotheses, purpose script, validity threats, no fake results.
expectations: Approach line names quantitative experimental family and a true experiment (random assignment is feasible)
Worldview is postpositivist
Output includes a quantitative purpose statement and H0/H1 whose variables match the purpose
Output does not report invented p-values, means, or participant quotes as if data were collected
Causal verbs are tied to the experimental design rather than to a survey

evals.prompt: I need a phenomenological study of the lived experience of night-shift nurses who lost hours after a hospital introduced a generative-AI triage assistant. Help me write the methodology: purpose, questions, design, and trustworthiness. No interviews have been run yet.
evals.expected_output: Qualitative phenomenology, constructivist (or transformative if framed as labor harm), purpose script, no hypotheses, interview protocol drafts, no fake themes.
expectations: Approach line names qualitative phenomenology
Worldview is constructivist or transformative, not postpositivist
Purpose statement follows the qualitative script (understand/explore/describe a central phenomenon for participants in a site)
Output has a central lived-experience question and no H0/H1
Output does not invent interview quotes, themes, or participant counts as completed data

evals.prompt: Necesito el estado del arte para el capítulo 2 de mi tesis sobre adopción de modelos de lenguaje en pymes manufactureras de Colombia 2019–2025. No voy a recoger entrevistas todavía; el entregable es la revisión.
evals.expected_output: Literature-review study with PRISMA-adapted counts, gap argument, not labeled mixed methods.
expectations: Design is named as narrative, scoping, or systematic review — not mixed methods, not phenomenology, not an experiment
Output includes Identification / Screening / Eligibility / Inclusion counts or an explicit in-progress count table
Literature is clustered into a gap argument rather than an annotated dump only
Output does not fabricate bibliographic entries for papers that were not retrieved

evals.expected_output: Short sourced definition. Does not enter Clarification Mode and does not run the eight-step loop.
expectations: Output answers the definitional question without entering Gate 0 Clarification Mode
Output does not run or announce the eight-step research loop
Output does not ship a protocol, consistency matrix, or study findings

evals.prompt: First measure how often warehouse pickers override the new routing algorithm, then interview high-override and low-override pickers to explain why. I need the study design, integration plan, and joint display. No data have been collected yet. Random assignment is not part of this study.
evals.expected_output: Mixed explanatory sequential (QUAN → qual), pragmatic worldview, integration question, joint display with pending cells, no invented numbers or quotes.
expectations: Approach line names mixed methods and explanatory sequential (QUAN → qual), not convergent and not a single-strand survey
Worldview is pragmatic (or transformative only if justice is the mixing reason)
Output includes a quantitative question, a qualitative question, and an integration question that refers to explaining the quantitative results
Output includes a joint display (or equivalent merge table) whose result cells are empty or marked pending
Output does not invent override rates, p-values, interview quotes, or themes as collected data
Qualitative sample is described as connecting from the quantitative results (high/low override), not as a second population estimate

evals.prompt: Design and evaluate a method for detecting silent data corruption in object-storage replicas. Build the method far enough to demonstrate on a worked instance and name how you will evaluate it against objectives. This is design science, not a survey of operators and not a Creswell mixed-methods study.
evals.expected_output: DSRM track: named artifact type, objectives, demonstration distinct from evaluation, Hevner method, no fake benchmarks, not labeled Creswell mixed methods.
expectations: Approach line names DSRM (Peffers/Hevner), not quantitative, qualitative, or mixed methods as the primary approach
Output names an artifact type (construct, model, method, or instantiation) and solution objectives
Demonstration (worked instance, tests, or walkthrough) is separate from evaluation against those objectives
A Hevner evaluation method is named (observational, analytical, experimental, testing, or descriptive) and residual user-side evaluation is listed if the agent cannot run it
Output does not invent runtime metrics, user counts, field deployments, or evaluation results that were not produced
Output does not label the study as Creswell mixed methods

evals.prompt: I want a phenomenological study of whether a four-day work week improves software-team defect rates compared with a five-day week. Use phenomenology. Write the methodology.
evals.expected_output: Mismatch flagged: phenomenology cannot license a causal defect-rate claim. Propose quantitative experimental/quasi. Do not silently execute phenomenology as the answer to the causal RQ.
expectations: Output flags a mismatch between the locked phenomenological design and the causal defect-rate question
Output proposes a Creswell-correct design in the quantitative experimental family (true or quasi) rather than obeying phenomenology as if it answered the causal RQ
Output states that a phenomenological study could claim lived experience of the four-day week, not a causal effect on defect rates
Output does not invent interview themes, essences, p-values, or defect-rate results as collected data
Output does not ship causal Findings under a phenomenology label

evals.prompt: Investiga si el emparejamiento por IA mejora la retención a 90 días de clientes de un SaaS B2B comparado con el emparejamiento manual. No tengo dataset ni puedo randomizar todavía. Quiero la respuesta ahora.
evals.expected_output: Experimental family named; no invented results; literature is not treated as the experiment; protocol + empty tables + pending fieldwork rather than a web synthesis as the causal answer.
expectations: Approach line names the quantitative experimental family (true or quasi); it does not relabel the study as a literature review in order to answer anyway
Findings do not claim that AI matching improves (or does not improve) 90-day retention as this study's causal result
Output does not invent p-values, retention rates, assignment, or participant counts as if an experiment ran
Literature, if used, is confined to the gap argument or background and is not presented as the experiment
Output ships a protocol (or equivalent) with empty result tables and an explicit pending-fieldwork list for assignment and measures
Causal verbs in any recommendation or discussion are labeled as unlicensed by this study's data
